stem: Name the Principal of M.A.O. College, Aligarh, who encouraged Muslim Communalism in the last decades of the 19th Century?
expl: M.A.O. College (Mohammadan Anglo-Oriental College), Aligarh, was founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. stem:
Consider the following events of Modern Indian History
1. Death sentence to Raja Nand Kumar
2. Treaty of Salbai
3. Battle of Wandiwash
4. Death of Tipu Sultan
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the above envents?
expl: The accepted years of these four events are as follows— Battle of Wandiwash – This was the decisive battle fought between the British and the French during the Third Carnatic War, which took place in 1760. This is the earliest event among the four. Death sentence to Raja Nandakumar – Raja Nandakumar, a high Brahmin of Bengal and former Diwan, was tried on the charge of forgery and hanged. This incident took place in 1775 in Calcutta. Treaty of Salbai – The agreement between the East India Company and the Marathas at the end of the First Anglo-Maratha War (1775–1782) is called the Treaty of Salbai. This treaty took place in 1782. Death of Tipu Sultan – Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore, was killed in the Battle of Srirangapatna during the Fourth Anglo–Mysore War (1799).

stem: Who was the secretary of Mahatma Gandhi during Noakhali?
expl: During the phase of violence in the Noakhali region of Bengal, Mahatma Gandhi’s personal secretary was the famous Bengali anthropologist and Gandhian leader Nirmal Kumar Bose. stem: The Bombay Plan proposed:

options.text: A rapid rate of economic growth

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The ‘Bombay Plan’ was presented in 1944 by a group of leading Indian industrialists. Under this plan, rapid economic growth of the Indian economy was advocated through proposals based on import substitution and industrialisation. At the same time, it reflected the need for state intervention and planned development in the country’s economic development, along with the need for public sector undertakings, which shows an abandonment of some capitalist features. On this basis, the correct answer will be option (e).

stem: Which Dogra general led successful military campaigns in Ladakh, Baltistan, and parts of Tibet between 1834 and 1841?
expl: Zorawar Singh, the commander-in-chief of Dogra ruler Gulab Singh of Jammu and Kashmir and the Governor of Kishtwar, led successful military campaigns in Ladakh, Baltistan and some parts of Tibet between 1834 and 1841. He was killed in battle during the Western Tibet campaign (1841). Under the Treaty of Amritsar (March 1846), the colonial rulers sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh rupees. Maharaja Gulab Singh unified Jammu and Kashmir.

stem:

III. The state of Kashmir signed the Instrument of Accession on 15-08-1947.

options.text: I, II, III and IV only

expl: Mir Laik Ali was the President of the Nizam’s Executive Council (the last Prime Minister of Hyderabad during the Nizam’s rule). ‘Operation Polo’ for Hyderabad’s merger with India took about five days in September 1948. The Maharaja of Kashmir, Hari Singh, signed the Instrument of Accession with India on 26 October 1947. Shah Nawaz Bhutto was the last Diwan of the Junagadh State. K.M. Munshi was appointed by the Government of India as its Agent General in the Hyderabad State. Thus, among the given statements, only I, IV and V are correct.

stem: First Indian elected to the British House of Commons was Dadabhai Naoroji who contested on the ticket of:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Dadabhai Naoroji (1825–1917) formed the London Indian Society in 1865 along with W. C. Banerjee. Its main objective was to increase political and social awareness among Indian students in England and to place India’s problems before the British public and the government. In 1892, he became the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons on the ticket of the Liberal Party. In his book “Poverty and Un-British Rule in India”, Dadabhai Naoroji clearly highlighted India’s economic distress during British rule, and he was the first to propound the Drain of Wealth, that is, the Drain Theory.

stem: Which famous Indian was known as 'Gurudev'?

On 23 December 1918, Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore laid the foundation of Visva-Bharati. In 1913, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for the English translation of his collection of songs “Gitanjali”, titled “Song Offerings”. He was known as “Gurudev”.

stem: Which woman made the most significant contribution to Indian politics after 1947?
expl: Aruna Asaf Ali was a nationalist and a freedom fighter. In the Quit India Movement of 1942, she and Sucheta Kriplani were two leading women organisers of the underground movement. After 1947, Aruna Asaf Ali joined the Socialist Party in 1948. In the 1950s, she joined the Communist Party of India and visited Moscow (Russia). In 1954, she was a collaborator in the formation of the National Federation of Indian Women. In 1958, she became the Mayor of Delhi, and in 1958 she also founded the newspaper ‘Patriot’. In this way, she made the maximum contribution to Indian politics after 1947.

stem: Who was the leader of the Non-Aligned Movement?
expl: The Non-Aligned Movement was started on India’s initiative. It may be noted that, to establish peace and mutual cooperation in the world, India’s Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, Egypt’s President Colonel Nasser, Ghana’s President Kwame Nkrumah, Indonesia’s President Sukarno, and Yugoslavia’s President Marshal Tito Josip Broz, with mutual cooperation, initiated the Non-Aligned Movement as a third force in world politics. The first summit of the non-aligned countries was held in Belgrade under the chairmanship of Yugoslavia’s President Marshal Tito. expl: The Panchsheel Agreement between India and China was signed on 29 April 1954. This agreement mentioned all the five principles of Panchsheel. The principles were— 1. Equality and mutual benefit, 5. Peaceful coexistence.

stem: Which is the oldest civilization in the world?
expl: The Mesopotamian civilization is considered the oldest civilization in the world. This civilization mainly developed in the regions of present-day Iraq, north-eastern Syria, south-eastern Turkey, and western Iran. The Egyptian civilization developed in the Nile river valley and is considered to be later than the Mesopotamian civilization.
